claims: Configured schema stores use the existing protocol-common ArtifactRef schema without exporting or changing a machine contract. Metadata, SHA-256, media type, schema dialect and exact byte length are checked. Pins and bytes are copied; returned bytes are checked again before UTF-8/JSON parsing.

Every schema read is authorized under copied Assistant, endpoint, session, environment and authority scope with deadline, cancellation and current-owner checks. Invocation arguments and extra invocation fields are not sent to the schema store. A reference, including a URL-like reference, never initiates networking or grants access.

Referenced snapshot definitions require both schema pins and agreement with the resolved schemas. Input access is checked again before admission. Missing stores, altered references, revoked access and inconsistent or incomplete definitions cannot fall back to the inline schema.

A fresh resolver recovers successful status using the original provider-bound output reference and authorized pinned bytes without discovery, admission or invocation. Registry byte reconstitution preserves the original schema independently of later discovery. Missing or tampered artifacts and changed owner scope withhold output.

Fixture results retain their original output schema reference. Changed or omitted references on a referenced invocation remain unknown after dispatch. Boolean and object JSON Schemas preserve their declared validation semantics.
